To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), you first need to find the derivative of the function, f'(x). Set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. The solutions to this equation are the x-values of the stationary points. To determine whether these points are maxima, minima, or points of inflection, you can use the second derivative test. Find the second derivative, f''(x), and evaluate it at the x-values of the stationary points. If f''(x) is positive, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) is negative, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) is zero, the test is inconclusive.
